20.0.s.en: (1) The seizing of Satan and the thousand-year reign

20.0.0.en: A new scene that St. John witnessed, his vision of a new angel coming down from heaven. Many interpreters believed that he is a symbol of Christ Himself, and others held that he is merely an angel commissioned by Christ to carry out His will ... and the scene in which the angel appeared shows the great mission he was commissioned to accomplish.

20.0.1.en: The key of the bottomless pit: a scene that suggests to us that the abyss is a place with doors, but the spiritual meaning intended is that the abyss, although it is the place of Satan and his followers, is under the absolute authority of God, who holds its key.

20.0.2.en: A great chain in his hand: a chain is used for binding criminals, and the whole scene is an entrance to what is coming.

20.1.0.en: The chain was used to bind Satan, and let us notice the use of four titles for the name of Satan at his seizure.

20.1.1.en: The dragon: it is the title of Satan in the Book of Revelation and means the chief of the demons, and among his followers were "the beast and the false prophet."

20.1.2.en: That old serpent: that is, the one who seduced Adam and Eve in Paradise long ago.

20.1.3.en: Satan: the most common name, and its meaning is the accuser and the envier of the children of God.

20.1.4.en: The devil: the enemy of all righteousness and goodness. See also the meanings in (ch. 12:9). The purpose of listing all these names is to confirm that the seizure of Satan has been accomplished and there is no room for doubt, and to bring the picture closer to our minds ... as when the daily newspapers write the news of the arrest of a criminal and mention his four-part name to confirm his identity.

20.1.5.en: Bound him a thousand years: this "thousand years" has stirred controversy over determining the earthly time of its beginning, and whether it has already happened or is yet to happen ...?! The well-known principle is that Holy Scripture is interpreted in the light of Holy Scripture; and because Christ Himself pointed to the time of the binding of Satan when He said:

20.1.6.en: "No man can enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man" (Mt 12:29). "I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven" (Lk 10:18). "Now shall the prince of this world be cast out" (Jn 12:31). Therefore the Church believes that this binding coincided with the Incarnation of Christ and the dispensation of His saving work on the wood of the Cross, and Satan, who used to bind people in ancient times (Lk 13:16), has become bound by the authority of Christ.

20.2.0.en: Cast him into the bottomless pit: that is, his kingdom (the abyss) became the place of his imprisonment.

20.2.1.en: Shut him up: a confirmation of God's authority and of the key that was with the angel.

20.2.2.en: Set a seal upon him: a pictorial expression meaning inability to come out and that no one is permitted to open for him. That he should deceive the nations no more: that is, the purpose of binding Satan is to give relative rest to the world after the multitude of his evils.

20.2.3.en: Till the thousand years should be fulfilled: the end of the thousand years is linked to the beginning of the signs of the Second Coming of the Lord Christ, and it was already pointed out that this thousand years is not earthly time.

20.2.4.en: The meaning intended from the whole verse is that the seizure of Satan has been accomplished by the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption of mankind, and his residence in the abyss has also been fixed, and Satan no longer has authority over man as he had, but his present presence in the abyss does not prevent him, even after his binding, from continuing his wars and spreading his thoughts and confusion and seduction. He is like one who barks behind walls, yet his barking still has an effect on many, frightening them and disturbing them and making them fall into various sins, but he no longer has the authority to take the believers to hell, the place of his kingdom, rather they enter the paradise of bliss, the place where the righteous wait, and it has become easy to overcome his wars by the power of Christ and the Cross.

20.2.5.en: He must be loosed a little season: that is, before the final coming of Christ he will also be permitted to wage his last war before his final judgment.

20.3.0.en: I saw thrones: that is, great heavenly seats.

20.3.1.en: They sat upon them: the Lord Christ promised the twelve to sit on thrones around Him in His Kingdom (Mt 19:28). And judgment was given unto them: connected with the same preceding promise, as the Lord Christ gave the Fathers the Apostles the right to pass judgments and judge the nations (Mt 19:28, 29). St. John tells us of two scenes in one picture: the first scene is the sitting of the Apostles and saints on thrones around His throne in the council of His rule, and the second scene concerns all the believers who enjoy being with Christ and accompanying Him in His glory. St. John specified for us that these people are those who did not worship the beast nor his image and did not receive his mark, and all this was discussed and explained before in (ch. 13:15-18), and the meaning intended is that none will reign with Christ except the one who resisted Satan and rejected him and overcame him.

20.4.0.en: But the rest of the dead: that is, the people who will not share with Christ in His reign and glory because they followed Satan and the mark of the beast and did not repent, and therefore they were described as the dead, that is, dead in God's sight spiritually even if they live on earth in their bodies.

20.4.1.en: Lived not again until the thousand years were finished: they did not repent and did not enjoy life with Christ in His Church on earth during earthly time, that is, the thousand years in which Christ reigns over the hearts of His children in the Church and those of them who have departed in the paradise of bliss. The meaning is that these wicked, that is, the spiritually dead, have no place in the Church or in Paradise, and this remains throughout the thousand years, that is, the period in which we live now, and the Holy Spirit calls everyone to rise from their death by faith in Christ and by attachment to the Church. This is the first resurrection: what is the meaning of the first resurrection, and what then is the second resurrection, and are there two resurrections of the bodies or what?..!

20.4.2.en: Because of the importance of this subject and its connection with the faith of the Church, we clarify the following:

20.4.3.en: 1- That there is only one resurrection of the bodies, and that is at the Second Coming of Christ and the end of life on earth and the beginning of the general judgment (Jn 5:28, 29, 2 Thess 1:8-10, 2 Pet 3:9).

20.4.4.en: 2- The meaning of the first resurrection is the spiritual resurrection, which is rising by repentance and Baptism from the death of sin, as Holy Scripture itself confirmed.

20.4.5.en: "And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; wherein in time past ye walked ... And hath raised us up together in Christ Jesus" (Eph 2:1-6). "Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God" (Col 2:12). "Whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die (rise) forever" (Jn 11:26). "We know that we have passed from death unto life (resurrection)" (1 Jn 3:14). From the foregoing the meaning of the first resurrection can be confirmed .. it is faith in the Lord Christ, rejection of Satan and resistance to him, receiving Baptism from the holy Church, and perseverance and striving to the last breath. As for the second resurrection, as we mentioned, it is the resurrection of the bodies on the day of judgment and entrance into the eternal Kingdom.

20.5.0.en: For this reason the one who had a part in the first resurrection deserved blessing and praise, "that is, the true, steadfast believers" who died to the desires of the world, so they rose and lived in the world with the mind of resurrection and victory.

20.5.1.en: The second death: the expression the second death can be understood in more than one way.

20.5.2.en: First: if the temporal death of the body is considered the first death, then the second death becomes an expression that signifies the eternal perdition of man.

20.5.3.en: Second: if the first death is considered the life of sin before repentance, then the second death becomes the temporal death of the body.

20.5.4.en: The meaning in either case is that whoever has the first resurrection in Christ by faith, Baptism and repentance will not be harmed at all by the temporal death of his body, as the Lord Christ said, "Fear not them which kill the body," since they have no authority over the spirit. For the spirit moves to Paradise and rejoices there and is not affected by the death of the body on earth, then it is immortal afterward in the eternal Kingdom after the Second Coming of Christ. On such the second death hath no power: a parenthetical sentence confirming that they will rise on the last day and reign forever with Christ. He means that the believers who will live by faith and repentance on earth will be priests of God on earth by the sacrifice of their souls.

20.5.5.en: They shall be priests of God and of Christ: another reason for their blessing and praise is that they were priests during their lives on earth by offering themselves and their will as a living daily sacrifice before God in their worship and service to Him, and they will also reign by their meekness and Christian conduct over the hearts of those who live with them (Mt 5:5) until the Second Coming of Christ, and the word thousand years here is symbolic, as we explained before that it includes the time from the Incarnation and redemption of Christ until near His Second Coming.

20.5.6.en: Beloved, be strong and take courage and remain firm in your first resurrection, and remember the promise of the Lord Christ that if you remain, the second death will not harm you and your soul will not perish. But to remain in this resurrection you must avoid all causes of spiritual death ... so flee from the enticements of the world and its desires and hold fast to your daily repentance, for repentance is your resurrection, and if you leave it, the second death will not leave you.

20.5.7.en: A review of our doctrine of the thousand years and the millennial reign of Christ:

20.5.8.en: While some (from other denominations) have gone in interpretation to say that the thousand years is a thousand literal years in which Christ will reign on earth and manage His affairs with His saints from Jerusalem, our Church rejects this teaching altogether for more than one reason:

20.5.9.en: 1- Christ Himself declared more than once that His kingdom is not of this world.

20.5.10.en: 2- Christ's announcement of His coming a second and final time, and this time witnesses the dissolution of nature and the falling of the planets and the end of life on earth (Mt 24).

20.5.11.en: 3- All the times and events in the Book of Revelation are symbolic events with spiritual meanings.. so why do we understand this particular time literally?.!

20.6.s.en: (2) Satan loosed for a little while

20.6.0.en: When the thousand years are expired: that is, near the end of earthly life and shortly before the Second Coming of the Lord Christ, and for a short period.

20.6.1.en: Shall be loosed out of his prison: that is, God permits him for a short period to use all his power and violence, and it will be a hard period in which he tries to lead the elect astray, but the power of God supports them so that they do not stumble.

20.7.0.en: These two verses make clear to us the last battle, which was mentioned without elaboration or detail.. and it can be described as follows:

20.7.1.en: 1- Satan goes out to gather his supporters for war from every corner of the world, "the four quarters of the earth."

20.7.2.en: 2- Their number was beyond counting and they surrounded the Church in a fierce war, for they came from the breadth of the earth with their evil to destroy the Church, "the camp of the saints and the beloved city."

20.7.3.en: 3- The end was swift and terrifying, for God sent down divine fire from heaven (the bowl of His wrath: ch. 16), and it devoured them all.

20.7.4.en: Gog and Magog: a figure for Satan and his helpers, but originally they were two kings of the northern kingdoms that fought and were hostile to Israel in ancient times, and about whom Ezekiel prophesied (Ezek 38:2) and about their severe destruction (Ezek 38:

20.8.0.en: As for their supreme commander and the manager of the whole kingdom of evil, who deceived and led many astray after him, his fate was eternal perdition in the lake of fire and brimstone, and his two companions also, his greatest helpers in the kingdom of evil, the beast and the false prophet.

20.8.1.en: As for their fate, it is final and eternal torment without ceasing or mercy, "day and night." And this is a declaration to us all that God's justice and vengeance on the wicked is coming .. coming however long He is patient with them. It is noted, dear reader, that after the end of this scene Satan and his helpers are not mentioned again.

20.8.2.en: The lake of fire and brimstone: it is the eternal place prepared for the torment of the wicked, and it is not hell and not the abyss either .. none of the wicked will enter this place before the coming of Christ and His judgment.

20.8.3.en: If many oppose you in your righteous conduct, do not be disturbed, and if they press you, whether those close to you or those in authority over you, to sin against God, do not agree with them, but obey the commandments of God before any man. Persevere in your striving, knowing that all evil will pass away and God will reward you in the end for your faithfulness, and will also support you in your confrontation with the world until you complete the days of your sojourn in peace.

20.9.0.en: And I saw: with this expression St. John moves us to the scene of the general and final judgment.. A great white throne: that is, the throne of Christ Himself, and he called it great to distinguish it from any other throne, such as the thrones of the disciples or the saints (v. 4). And whiteness signifies absolute purity and cleanness, which God alone possesses.

20.9.1.en: The earth and the heaven fled away: they passed away and had no place or life, and heaven here means the heaven of the stars and planets.

20.9.2.en: The scene here is frightening and awesome, as Christ Himself sat on His throne of judgment, pure and holy and just, after all the signs of the material world known to us had passed away, and we had entered the time of endless eternity.

20.10.0.en: All the dead appeared before the throne, risen in their new bodies, from the greatest of them to the smallest, for the resurrection is for all, even for children.

20.10.1.en: The books were opened: that is, the books that contained and recorded the works of each one of them were opened.

20.10.2.en: The book of life: another book was opened in which were written the names of the heirs of eternal life.

20.10.3.en: The dead were judged: each one was called to account for all the works he did in his life, which were written in the books, since everything was recorded.

20.10.4.en: According to their works: that is, not according to their positions or great duties on earth but according to their works, in agreement with or contrary to the commandments of Christ.

20.10.5.en: St. John describes how the judgment is carried out, for on the day of judgment each person is confronted with all his works that he did consciously and knowingly, whether small or great, for everything that man did not repent of is recorded against him and kept, and he cannot deny it or justify it.

20.11.0.en: The sea gave up the dead: the direct meaning is that whoever died by drowning in the sea and was not buried rose also.

20.11.1.en: Death and hell: that is, whoever was dead and held in hell rose also from death for judgment.

20.11.2.en: The general meaning of this verse is that since God alone is the One who has authority over all creation and commanded the beginning of the judgment, all the bodies rose regardless of where they were or where they were buried and were united with the spirits so that the judgment may be carried out according to God's just decree and He gives each one according to his work. This verse comes depicting the sea and the abyss as persons, guards who were entrusted with the spirits and bodies, and now the time has come for their handing them over for judgment.

20.12.0.en: Because death and hell are bound up with sin, they became enemies of God, as St. Paul said, "The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death" (1 Cor 15:26), and because after the resurrection there will be no other death and no need of the abyss (the place where the wicked or Satan wait), God cast them also into the lake, which is the lake of eternal torment mentioned in (v. 10). This is the second death: that is, this is the death and eternal perdition after which there is no life or resurrection, and it is the perpetual torment in the lake of fire and brimstone, and it is extremely horrible.

20.13.0.en: That is, whoever had no good life or constant repentance and by his evil works refused to have his name written in the book of the eternal inheritance (the book of life) became rejected and was cast into the lake, just as the dragon, the beast and the false prophet and all the followers of evil, and death and hell, were cast, for the fate is one for all the wicked.

20.13.1.en: My beloved God, the scene of judgment is a very terrifying scene, at which the soul trembles and fears, so keep it present before me always, my God, that I may not be negligent nor turn aside to a life of evil, and make me always pray with Your Church the Prayer of the Veil (from the Agpeya), saying: "Your judgment is fearful, when men are gathered and the angels stand. The books are opened, the deeds are revealed and the thoughts are examined. What judgment will be mine, who am convicted by my sins; who will quench my darkness if You do not have mercy on me, O Lord? For You are compassionate toward mankind.

20.13.2.en: The new heaven and the new earth: introduction to the chapter: after Satan and his helpers and all the wicked are cast into the lake burning with fire and brimstone, and the scene of judgment, the Spirit moves us to a wonderful scene, which is His speaking about the Kingdom of Heaven and the meeting of Christ with His holy children.
